t: Learn About Expressions of Ability and Potential Verbs in Japanese
s: April 30, 2025 - For example, the speaker of the question "can you buy the tickets?" probably doesn't doubt that the person he is speaking to is physically able to buy the tickets. It's intended to ask whether the person has enough money, or whether the person will take care of this task on the speaker's behalf. In Japanese, attaching the phrase koto ga dekiru （～ことができる）after the basic form of the verb is one way to express ability or qualification to do something.
